key_insight: A dual topological-derivative framework simultaneously creates holes for topology optimization and estimates crack-driving energy release rates from a single enriched analysis, enabling fracture-aware design of 3-D brittle solids.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to redesign brittle structures, such as L-brackets, to reduce fracture risk while maintaining computational efficiency in 3-D optimization.
method: Level-set topology is parameterized with radial basis functions and updated via topology optimization.
An interface-enriched finite element model computes the structural response on the uncracked geometry.
Dual topological derivatives are used both for hole nucleation and for boundary ERR evaluation, with non-local stress recovery and a p-mean objective aggregation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 3-D numerical examples, including the standard L-bracket benchmark, to demonstrate the framework's fracture-mitigation capability.
watch_item: ERR predictions depend strongly on stress accuracy, so the non-local stress-recovery step and enriched-node placement are important implementation sensitivities.
paper_title: $\partial^2 ( \mathrm{TO} ) $: A Dual Topological Derivative-Based Enriched Topology Optimization for Fracture Mitigation in 3-D Brittle Solids
